decisions.reason: The supplement range builds on the established Trivital line and costs little to keep in pharmacies, so the option remains worth holding.
The skin and hair supplement fits the existing pharmacy channel with low carrying cost and no negative signals, so keeping it preserves upside.
Joint health is a steady demand segment and the product was promoted to its own page, so it is cheap to keep and has potential.
The mushroom-based immune concept is more niche but likely gained from pandemic-era immune demand, and its low carrying cost justifies holding the option.
The generic valsartan is distant from the core and was hit by the 2018 contamination recall in a low-margin market, but a resupplied product has modest carrying cost, so it stays under close review.
The OTC triptan is a differentiated consumer-health product consistent with the firm's portfolio broadening, and its prospects have not yet resolved negatively.
